group.name: Cisco IOS XR Receiver
group.description: Operational dashboards for Cisco IOS XR gNMI and MDT telemetry collected by the Cisco OS receiver.

variables.description: YANG module that produced the datapoint.
gNMI dial-in or MDT dial-out transport.

dashboards.name: 00 IOS XR Telemetry Trust And Coverage
dashboards.description: Value: verifies that IOS XR subscriptions are connected, fresh, decodable, and within configured path and cardinality limits.
dashboards.value: Use this dashboard before interpreting router telemetry. It distinguishes an IOS XR incident from a receiver connection, model compatibility, freshness, or datapoint-limit problem.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains the IOS XR collection-trust workflow. Interpretation: prove that subscriptions and updates are healthy, then investigate decode failures, unsupported paths, reconnects, compact GPB payloads, and dropped datapoints before trusting model-specific dashboards.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Start here whenever IOS XR data is missing, stale, or surprising. Healthy targets have active subscriptions, a continuing update rate, and an advancing last-success timestamp. Decode errors, unsupported paths, compact GPB payloads, or cardinality drops mean model data can be incomplete even while a connection is alive.

charts.name: Active Subscriptions
charts.description: Value: identifies IOS XR targets with an active telemetry subscription. Interpretation: a missing or zero row means that target is not currently delivering telemetry and downstream charts should not be treated as authoritative.

charts.name: Updates And Reconnects
charts.description: Value: correlates incoming update volume with connection instability. Interpretation: a steady update rate is expected for streaming targets; reconnect growth or an update rate falling to zero points to transport, authentication, certificate, or router availability trouble.

charts.name: Decode Path And Cardinality Exceptions
charts.description: Value: exposes conditions that make an otherwise connected IOS XR feed incomplete. Interpretation: rising decode errors indicate payload incompatibility; unsupported paths indicate model gaps; dropped datapoints indicate that path or target scope exceeds the configured guardrail.

charts.name: Compact GPB Payloads
charts.description: Value: shows payloads received in compact GPB form that the generic decoder cannot expand into YANG metrics. Interpretation: any sustained rate means collection is alive but model telemetry is being counted rather than decoded; use KV-GPB or add model-specific protobuf support.

charts.name: Last Successful Update
charts.description: Value: finds targets whose last visible datapoint is stale. Interpretation: the Unix timestamp should advance with incoming telemetry; compare it to current time and use reconnect and decode panels when it stops moving.

dashboards.name: 01 IOS XR Interfaces Optics And Physical Path
dashboards.description: Value: connects interface state, traffic, errors, discards, packet volume, MTU, and available IOS XR optics telemetry for physical-path triage.
dashboards.value: Use this dashboard when an IOS XR path is down, lossy, silent, asymmetric, or capacity constrained. It keeps interface state and counters together so operators can identify the affected router and interface before moving into model-specific optics evidence.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains the IOS XR interface and physical-path workflow. Interpretation: begin with admin and operational state, then correlate octet, packet, error, and discard rates; use MTU and native optics path data to test configuration and physical-layer hypotheses.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this page for interface and physical-path incidents. It is based on the receiver's default OpenConfig interface path, so traffic and health charts remain portable across IOS XR releases. Enable the optional `optics` path group when native transceiver detail is required.

charts.name: Interface Administrative And Operational State
charts.description: Value: identifies interfaces that are disabled, down, or in an unexpected state. Interpretation: compare admin and operational state per interface; admin-up and oper-down points to a physical, peer, optic, or lower-layer issue.

charts.name: Interface Octet Rate
charts.description: Value: compares ingress and egress traffic to find silence, asymmetry, or a change around an incident. Interpretation: an unexpected zero, one-way traffic, or a sharp rate change should be correlated with state, errors, discards, and peer-side evidence.

charts.name: Interface Packet Rate
charts.description: Value: shows packet pressure and direction independently of frame size. Interpretation: packet-rate spikes with modest octet rate can reveal small-packet load, while one-sided or absent packet flow narrows the affected direction.

charts.name: Interface Errors And Discards
charts.description: Value: distinguishes corrupt or failed traffic from congestion, queue, or policy drops. Interpretation: errors point toward the physical path or framing; discards with clean error counters point toward capacity, buffering, policy, or forwarding behavior.

charts.name: Interface MTU
charts.description: Value: exposes MTU differences that can explain selective reachability, fragmentation, or application-specific loss. Interpretation: compare MTU across both ends of the path and with the encapsulation requirement when only larger packets fail.

dashboards.name: 02 IOS XR Routing MPLS SR And Time Sync
dashboards.description: Value: provides a model-aware landing page for IOS XR route inventory and optional BGP, ISIS, MPLS, segment-routing, NTP, and PTP path groups.
dashboards.value: Use this dashboard after collection trust is established to confirm which control-plane model groups are producing telemetry and to inspect IPv4 route inventory. Detailed leaf names vary by IOS XR release, so the coverage panels intentionally use receiver-provided YANG module and path dimensions.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use optional IOS XR control-plane path groups without mistaking absent configuration for receiver failure. Interpretation: validate update and model coverage first, then use route counts and module-specific filters to focus on BGP, ISIS, MPLS, segment routing, NTP, or PTP telemetry enabled for the target.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
IOS XR native YANG leaves are normalized under `cisco.iosxr.yang.<module>...`. Enable only the path groups supported by the router and needed by the operating model. Use the YANG Module filter to isolate BGP, ISIS, MPLS, segment-routing, NTP, or PTP data, and return to the telemetry-trust dashboard if a selected group produces no updates.

charts.name: IPv4 RIB Routes By Protocol
charts.description: Value: tracks route inventory by the protocol and table dimensions exported by the IOS XR IPv4 RIB model. Interpretation: abrupt route-count loss or unexpected divergence between protocols should be correlated with neighbor and adjacency state on the router.

charts.name: Control Plane Update Flow
charts.description: Value: confirms that the telemetry stream continues to carry control-plane model updates during the selected window. Interpretation: filter by router and YANG module, then treat a flat zero alongside active subscriptions as an on-change quiet period or a path/model selection issue rather than immediate proof of routing failure.

charts.name: Unsupported Control Plane Paths
charts.description: Value: identifies configured model paths that a router does not advertise or accept. Interpretation: filter to the affected router and compare its IOS XR release and capabilities before enabling BGP, ISIS, MPLS, segment-routing, NTP, or PTP groups fleet-wide.

charts.name: Control Plane Decode Failures
charts.description: Value: surfaces native or OpenConfig payloads that could not be translated into metrics. Interpretation: a rise after a router upgrade or path-group change points to a schema, encoding, or payload compatibility issue and means routing dashboards may be incomplete.
